Definition: from the base of G297 and G3598; a fork in the road:--where two ways meet.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the story of the colt: the disciples found it tied by the door without, in a place where two ways meet, and they loosed him. It is a fork in the road — a crossroads outside the village — and the detail is there because the colt was waiting exactly where Jesus said it would be.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a crossroads carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the detail — the colt tied where two ways meet, just as Jesus had told them.
